{{nihongo|'''Tabe Shrine'''|太部神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kawabe, Gifu|arz|كوابه|ceb|Kawabe-chō|es|Kawabe (Gifu)|fa|کاوابه، گیفو|fr|Kawabe|it|Kawabe|ja|川辺町|ko|가와베정|ms|Kawabe, Gifu|my|ခါဝဘဲမြို့၊ ဂိဖု|pl|Kawabe (Gifu)|ru|Кавабе|tl|Kawabe, Gifu|tr|Kawabe|uk|Кавабе|ur|کاوا بے، گیفو|uz|Kavabe (Gifu)|zh|川邊町|qid=Q1203748}}, {{ill|Kamo District, Gifu|ceb|Kamo-gun (distrito sa Hapon, Gifu-ken)|es|Distrito de Kamo (Gifu)|fr|District de Kamo (Gifu)|id|Distrik Kamo, Gifu|it|Distretto di Kamo (Gifu)|ja|加茂郡|ko|가모군 (기후현)|pl|Powiat Kamo|pt|Distrito de Kamo|th|อำเภอคาโมะ|uk|Повіт Камо (Ґіфу)|vi|Kamo (quận)|zh|加茂郡|qid=Q1348656}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}}. {{nihongo|'''Tabe Shrine'''|太部神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

It is a candidate shrine (ronsha) for Tabe Shrine in Kamo District, {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha register}}. Another theory identifies Tabe Shrine as {{ill|Tabekoten Shrine|Q11444530|qid=Q11444530}} in the same Kawabe town. Its {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former rank}} was village shrine.

It is about 800 m east of {{ill|Shinyamakawa Bridge|Q11502002|qid=Q11502002}} over the {{ill|Hida River|Q3366160|qid=Q3366160}}.

== Overview ==
The founding period is unknown. It was originally enshrined in a different location, but after being destroyed by fire it was relocated and rebuilt at the present site. The date of the fire and rebuilding is unknown, but a wooden plaque inscribed with {{ill|1576|Q6700|qid=Q6700}} ({{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 4) remains, and there is a construction record for {{ill|1639|Q6897|qid=Q6897}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}} 16), so the fire is presumed to have occurred between the {{ill|Muromachi period|ar|فترة In the Edo period it was called Taibonten'ō-gū. In the Meiji period it was renamed Tabe Shrine.
